explanation: Silver nitrate reacts with sodium chloride to form insoluble silver chloride, which precipitates out of solution, and sodium nitrate.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: Two colourless solutions: silver nitrate and sodium chloride.
beaker_view.final_appearance: A colourless solution with a white, curdy precipitate suspended in it, settling out over time.
beaker_view.observation: The instant the two colourless solutions are mixed, a dense white precipitate appears throughout the liquid — the standard test for chloride ions.
